title: Adaptive Pin Pattern Modification on Standard Cells Towards ECO Routing
problem: Pin inaccessibility on standard cells causes routing failures in deep-submicron physical design, with failures increasing as cell sizes shrink.
motivation: Resolving pin accessibility failures post-placement enables successful ECO routing without redesign, critical for meeting complex timing closure requirements.
method: When chip designers route wires connecting components, they sometimes can't reach the connection points (pins) on standard cells—the pre-built components used throughout a chip. This system fixes routing failures by adaptively modifying pins on problem cells using three techniques: pin-shift-trim (moving and shortening pins), pin-free (removing pins entirely), and pin-bridge (creating bridges between pins). For each cell that has a routing failure, it tries these modifications and uses maze routing (a pathfinding algorithm that explores paths around obstacles) to find working connections.
key_novelty: Adaptive pin pattern modifications to individual cells enable late-stage routing changes (ECO) with no impact on performance, power, or area—116x faster than competing multi-commodity flow methods.
contributions: Three pin-pattern modification techniques (PST, PF, PB) for routing flexibility
Adaptive selection scheme matching modifications to cell instance failures
ECO router resolving 17.7% of previously unfixable pin inaccessibility cases
Orders-of-magnitude speedup vs. concurrent optimization methods

metrics.accuracy: resolves 17.7% of pin inaccessibility cases vs. commercial tool

limitations: Technique only applicable to post-placement ECO routing scenarios; does not address root cause of pin accessibility in cell design.
primary_theme: adaptive pin modification for ECO routing
